jess: Heads up — saw a rare correctness case hitting prod during a prefetched-prefix demote + immediate repopulate. Essentially read-after-demote returned stale values for ~200 requests in a 3m window. Not reproducible locally yet. :worried:

jess: Quick sketch: when we demote a prefix we currently mark it evicted and let inflight refs drain; but repopulate can race and reinsert a different entry while old read paths still have vague assumptions about residency.

lina: can you paste the log snippet?

jess: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] demote(prefix=a/b/c) mark=draining epoch=42
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] read(prefix=a/b/c) hit entry@slot123 residency=0 epoch=41
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] repopulate(prefix=a/b/c) insert entry@slot456 epoch=43
```

raj: so the read saw residency==0 but still considered item valid? that sounds like a small window where residency transitions but read path doesn't verify identity.

akshay: yep. two options: 1) add an ownership_epoch on slot header and make read check epoch==container_epoch, or 2) make demote a two-phase operation with an explicit fence that prevents reinserts until drain completes.

lina: epoch sounds simpler to migrate; fence blocks reinserts which hurts throughput for hot prefixes. epoch avoids global stalls but needs compact storage and careful wraparound handling.

jess: proposal: add 32-bit ownership_epoch in slab metadata. On demote we increment container_epoch -> mark draining -> wait for inflight refs, then reap. Reads validate entry. Repopulate sets entry. If epochs mismatch read treats as miss and falls back to miss-path / fetch.

raj: wraparound on 32-bit is low risk but should we use 64-bit? cost vs benefit?

akshay: 32-bit should be fine given monotonic increments are rare (demotes per slot). We can also reserve high-bit as special tombstone if needed. 64-bit doubles metadata size and may hurt cache density on hot slabs.

lina: important integration point: snapshots / cold restore. We need to persist epoch with snapshot so restored nodes don't accidentally accept stale entries from another epoch.

jess: agreed. snapshot proto change: include container_epoch per slab. Migration plan: default to 0; feature-gate reads to check epoch only if feature flag enabled. For rollout: enable on canary, collect errors and miss-rate deltas, then widen.

akshay: perf: read path adds one cmp to check epoch field. we should microbench. also ensure we don't do atomic ops on hot path if not necessary — plain load of metadata is fine under our memory model.

raj: metrics to add: demote_epoch_rolls, read_epoch_mismatch_count, repopulate_wait_time, blocked_repop_in_progress. Also a sampler to capture offending traces.

lina: how about correctness proof sketch? If each entry carries owner_epoch and container holds current_epoch, any entry from an older epoch will be rejected. Invariant: after container_epoch increments, no read can succeed against pre-increment entries. Demote flow: increment -> mark draining -> wait inflight->reap. That satisfies it.

jess: edge-case: concurrent demote + repop: repop must write entry with current_epoch. If repop wins before drain finishes, old read paths will still reject because epoch changed. So okay.

akshay: migration steps: (1) add epoch field with default 0, (2) add read check behind feature flag, (3) implement demote increments behind same flag, (4) canary and perf run. rollback trivial (flip flag).

raj: one more: eviction/packing background job that compacts slab must preserve epoch semantics. If we move entries between slots, copy epoch. If we reuse slot, initialize epoch to container_epoch.

lina: implementation note: store container_epoch in the slab header and per-entry owner_epoch as u32. To reduce noise, only check epoch for entries with residency<=1 (i.e., recently demoted hotspots) — but that's heuristic and may miss cases. I'd start conservative (check all) then optimize post-canary.

jess: agree on conservative start. I'll prototype the slab header + read check in a branch and drop microbench results here. TL;DR decision: go epoch-based demote fencing behind feature flag, 32-bit owner_epoch in slab metadata, persist epoch in snapshots, add metrics and samplers.

infra-bot: deploy-ci: jess/epoch-proto branch created, CI queued. :rocket:

lina: great. please include a short migration checklist in the PR description (snapshots, snapshot-version bump, feature flag flips, canary instructions).

jess: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
